title: Skip-Gen Travel in Asia
excerpt: Skip-gen travel — grandparents traveling with grandchildren — is Asia's hottest luxury trend. Here's what's driving it, the best destinations, and the resorts rolling out the red carpet for three generations.
author: The Luxury Explorer
content:
What Is Skip-Gen Travel?

Skip-gen travel — or 'grandcations' — is the fastest-growing segment in family luxury travel. It's exactly what it sounds like: grandparents taking their grandchildren on trips, deliberately skipping the middle generation. In 2026, this trend has exploded across Asia. Hilton's 2026 Trends Report found that 60% of APAC families are planning skip-generation trips, and 89% believe these journeys significantly enhance grandparents' health and wellbeing.

The reasons are as heartwarming as they are practical. Grandparents have more flexibility in retirement and often greater disposable income. Grandchildren have school holidays that create natural travel windows. And parents — exhausted from the logistics of family life — are increasingly enthusiastic about sending their kids on luxury adventures with grandparents who have the time, patience, and resources to create truly special experiences.

Why Asia Leads the Skip-Gen Revolution

Asia's Hospitality DNA

Asian luxury resorts have an instinctive understanding of multi-generational dynamics that Western hotels often miss. Staff at top properties treat grandparents with genuine deference while engaging children with warmth and patience. This is cultural — Asian societies inherently respect and celebrate the grandparent-grandchild bond. Resorts don't just accommodate skip-gen pairs; they actively design experiences around them.

The 'Inheritourism' Factor

Hilton's research coined 'inheritourism' to describe how younger generations are inheriting travel preferences from their parents and grandparents. 73% of travelers say their travel style was shaped by their parents. Skip-gen trips are the most intense form of this — grandchildren directly absorbing grandparents' appreciation for quality, service, and cultural richness. These shared experiences create lifelong brand loyalty to specific destinations, hotels, and travel styles.

Safety and Ease of Travel

Asia is exceptionally safe for skip-gen pairs. Singapore, Japan, South Korea, and the luxury enclaves of Thailand and Bali consistently rank among the safest destinations worldwide. For grandparents concerned about managing a trip alone with grandchildren, the combination of safety, English-speaking service staff, and 24-hour concierge support provides genuine peace of mind.

Top Skip-Gen Destinations in Asia

1. Singapore: The Perfect First Skip-Gen Trip

Singapore is the ideal launch destination for skip-gen travel. It's compact, safe, and English-speaking with extraordinary attractions designed for interactive learning. Gardens by the Bay, the S.E.A. Aquarium, and the Singapore Zoo are world-class and easily navigated without a car. The Marina Bay Sands offers interconnecting rooms and a dedicated family pool area. For cultural moments, the Peranakan Museum offers workshops where grandfathers and grandkids can learn traditional craft together. The Marina One complex has beautiful gardens that offer a quiet retreat after busy sightseeing days.

Best resort for skip-gen: The Fullerton Bay Hotel — the heritage story engages grandparents, the rooftop pool captivates kids, and the Raffles Place location means walking access to most attractions.

2. Bali: Culture, Nature, and the Ultimate Kids' Club

Bali offers skip-gen pairs the opportunity to combine cultural immersion with pure resort relaxation. The island's health and wellness orientation means grandparents feel energized rather than exhausted, while kids are captivated by the island's unique culture — temple visits, rice terrace walks, and creative workshops.

Best resort for skip-gen: Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan. The Kids for All Seasons program offers Balinese craft workshops, rice pady walks, and cooking classes — all facilitated by staff who understand the skip-gen dynamic. Grandparents can participate or retreat to the Ayung Spa while kids are engaged nearby.

3. Japan: Order, Safety, and Lifelong Memories

Japan is ideal for skip-gen trips focused on cultural discovery. The order, cleanliness, and extreme safety mean grandparents don't worry about logistics. The bullet train system makes multi-city itineraries manageable without flights. And Japan's veneration of elders means grandparents are treated with exceptional respect wherever they go — from ryokan inns to Michelin restaurants.

Best resort for skip-gen: Aman Tokyo or Hoshinoya Tokyo. Aman's spacious suites and 29th-floor pool work for both generations; Hoshinoya's traditional ryokan experience is an education in Japanese culture that grandparents and grandkids explore together. Guided kimono-wearing sessions and tea ceremonies are shared experiences that create lasting memories.

4. Malaysia: Luxury Nature Adventures

Langkawi and Penang offer skip-gen pairs a mix of nature, heritage, and luxury at exceptional value. The Datai Langkawi's Discovery Centre runs guided rainforest walks where grandparents learn alongside grandchildren. In Penang, the George Town heritage zone offers food tours that work for adventurous eaters of all ages, and the street art trail is an engaging self-guided activity. Batu Ferringhi Beach has a night market perfect for the \"choose one souvenir\" tradition skip-gen pairs often develop.

Best resort for skip-gen: The Datai Langkawi — the nature immersion, family spa treatments, and guided night walks are designed for intergenerational discovery. The separate villa accommodation means grandparents can have quiet evenings after the grandkids are asleep.

Skip-Gen Packages Worth Knowing About

  • Club Med 'Skip-Gen' Package — Club Med's luxury resorts in Phuket, Bali, and Cherating offer dedicated skip-gen programs with activities designed for grandparent-grandchild pairs. Pricing includes all meals, activities, and kids' club. From $180/person/night
  • Kensington Tours 'Generations' Collection — Private guided tours with guides trained in intergenerational travel. They adjust pacing, provide enrichment for both ages, and handle all logistics so the pair focuses on bonding
  • Six Senes 'Live Genuinely' Multi-Gen — Six Senses properties across Asia offer interconnecting suites, family wellness programs, and dedicated hosts for multi-generational groups. The Earth Lab activities (composting, beekeeping, organic gardening) engage kids while grandparents enjoy the spa

Skip-Gen Travel Tips from Experienced Grandparents

  • Pack for your grandchild first, then yourself — Kids need more changes of clothes, entertainment materials, and comfort items than adults. Pack their essentials in your carry-on, yours in checked luggage
  • Build in rest time every day — Even the most energetic grandchild needs downtime. Two planned activities per day maximum. The rest is for swimming, reading, and spontaneous connection
  • Choose resorts with kids' clubs that operate until evening — Grandparents need genuine rest time too. Resorts with kids' clubs open until 9pm-plus (like Trisara and Four Seasons Bali) allow for separate dinner or spa time
  • Create a daily 'grandparent time' ritual — Whether it's a pre-breakfast walk on the beach or a bedtime story on the balcony, a recurring daily ritual creates the emotional anchor for the entire trip
  • Document everything — These trips create some of the most cherished family photographs. Consider hiring a local photographer for one morning rather than relying on selfies
The Luxury Family Verdict: Skip-gen travel in Asia is not just a trend — it's a movement that's reshaping how families connect across generations. The combination of Asia's world-class luxury infrastructure, instinctive hospitality culture, and diverse destinations creates the perfect environment for grandparent-grandchild adventures. Whether it's a cultural journey through Japan, a beach retreat in Phuket, or a discovery trip to Bali's temples, the experiences created on skip-gen trips become the stories told at family gatherings for decades. Budget $3,000-8,000 per grandparent-grandchild pair for a 7-day trip depending on destination and accommodation tier.
